neutral_facts.value: The accused caused the death of the deceased by hitting him with a stone. There was a prior incident of altercation between the deceased and the accused, which established motive. Witnesses testified that the accused and the deceased were seen together before the incident, and that the accused was seen beating the deceased with a stone. The deceased's injuries were severe, with multiple wounds and disfigured facial features, indicating a fatal injury. The medical report suggested that the injuries were inflicted with full force, and there was no evidence to suggest a free fight. The accused claimed it was a sudden fight, but the courts found this not credible.

prosecution_argument.value: The prosecution argued that the accused-appellant was responsible for causing the death of the deceased, supported by reliable evidence of witnesses, including PW 3 and PW 4, and PW 7's account of the earlier incident furnishing motive. The evidence indicated prior enmity and that the injuries on the deceased suggested intention to cause death.

quotes.text: Evidence of witnesses with regard to earlier incident of altercation between deceased and the accused-appellant furnishing motive to the accused - There was previous enmity - Evidence of eye witnesses supporting the prosecution case and found reliable - It was not case of sudden fight or sudden provocation or in the heat of passion- There was enough evidence to prove that appellant was responsible for causing death of the deceased.
The view taken by the courts below was certainly a possible view for accepting the evidence led by the prosecution in support of its version.

defence_argument.value: The defence argued that the case fell under Exception 4 to Section 300 of the Penal Code, as it was a case of sudden fight, and that the injuries on the accused indicated a free fight. They also claimed the accused was falsely implicated.

quotes.text: The defence version of the accused was not found to be reliable.

The accused in his statement under 313 Cr.P.C. took the plea that he was falsely implicated as he was member of Yuvak Gram Kalyan Samiti and he had made complaint to the District Magistrate against illegal distillation of liquor which made the police inimical to him.

legal_principle_applied.value: The Supreme Court applied the principle that the determination of whether a case falls under Section 302 or 304 of the Penal Code depends on various factors, including the nature of the weapon, the circumstances of the incident, and whether the attack was in the heat of passion or with prior enmity.

quotes.text: Question whether a case fell under Section 302 or 304 has to be decided from case to case depending on factors like the circumstances in which the incident takes place, the nature of weapon used and whether weapon was carried or was taken from the spot and whether the assault was aimed on vital part of the body; the amount of force used; whether the deceased participated in the sudden fight; whether there was any previous enmity; whether there was any sudden provocation; whether the attack was in the heat of passion; whether the person inflicting the injury took any undue advantage or acted in a cruel or unusual manner.
The list of circumstances is not exhaustive and there may be several other circumstances with reference to individual cases.

sentencing_rationale.value: The final sentence of life imprisonment was imposed because the accused was found responsible for causing the death of the deceased, with the injuries indicating intention to cause death or a fatal injury, and there was no evidence of free fight or sudden provocation.

quotes.text: There was enough evidence to prove that the accused appellant was responsible for causing the death of the deceased.
In these circumstances, we do not find any ground to interfere.

judicial_aggravating_factors.value: Prior enmity, the nature of injuries on the deceased suggesting intention to cause death, and the accused acting in a cruel manner.

quotes.text: The nature of injuries suffered by the deceased did not show that the injury was suffered accidentally. There were multiple wounds and the face was disfigured. The bones are pulverized. The brain matter was flowing out from all wounds.
Seen in the light of previous motive, the accused can be said to have caused the death by acting in a cruel manner.
